nilReasons.documentation: A well-formed operand outside the operation's domain — the canonical case is SQRT of a negative rational; NIL-REASON asked of a value that is not a NIL is another.
A well-formed index or count outside the addressed collection's bounds, answered as a projection rather than a raise.
Text that does not denote a value in the operation's target encoding — NUM applied to text outside the sealed numeric grammar, or JSON-DECODE applied to text that is not one JSON value.
A NIL the program wrote rather than computed: the NIL Word, or NIL inside a vector literal. Not produced by any Word's projection.

A lookup found nothing at what it was asked for: a key a Record does not hold (GET, WITHOUT), a value a Vector does not contain (INDEX-OF, BSEARCH), a needle a text does not contain (SEARCH), or a name no Word answers to (CONTRACT).

A well-formed generative operation (RANGE, FILL, RESHAPE) whose materialized result would exceed the space water level. The only reason that projects rather than raises even for a request that could never fit.

An absence the program declared itself with ABSENT. The registered reason is this one id; the text the program gave is carried on the value as its detail and is what NIL-REASON answers, so the reason space is closed here and open there — the first parameterized reason, recorded as such.

errorCategories.documentation: A higher-order Word's block operand did not return the shape its contract requires — MAP/FILTER/FOLD/SCAN's block returned other than one value per contract.

An ERROR the program raised itself with FAIL: a user Word saying that a call to it is wrong, with the program's own text as the message. The category is this one id; the text is a message, and like every message it is not a machine-readable surface.

DEF or DEL asked for a dictionary change its existing bindings refuse: DEF named a word the dictionary already binds in a way this definition cannot resolve, or DEL named a word other words still reference.

RECORD was given a key Vector in which some key appears twice. A Record holds each key once (LANG.RECORDS.STRUCTURE), and which of two values should win is a decision the program has not made, so the Word raises rather than keeping either.
The total execution-step budget was exhausted before the program finished.
An operand that must be a whole number is not one: an index (GET, PUT), a count (TAKE, DROP, COLLECT, FORMAT's digits — a count that cannot be negative is also refused below zero), or a RANGE bound.
DEF was given a body that is not a well-formed definition: not a Vector, or an empty one.
DEF, DEL or BIND was given a name that cannot be a name at all (empty, wrong lexical shape).
A shape operand (FILL, RESHAPE) is not a shape — a Vector of non-negative integers, the image of SHAPE — or, for RESHAPE, is one whose product is not the leaf count.
Program text that does not parse — an unclosed block, a | outside a clause, a mismatched delimiter.

A binding and a Word were asked to share a name: BIND to a name a Word holds, or DEF to a name a live binding holds. The two name spaces are disjoint by rule (LANG.DICTIONARY.RESOLUTION), so this is one condition from either side.

A Record Word (KEYS, VALUES, WITHOUT, HAS?, MERGE) was given something other than a Record where one is required. A Record is its own domain (LANG.VALUES.DISJOINT): a Vector of pairs is not a Record and nothing converts one implicitly.
An operand the Word reads as a container — GET and PUT, which read and write a Vector at an index or a Record at a key — is neither a Vector nor a Record.
An operand the Word reads as a Scalar is not one: arithmetic on a non-number, or an order asked of something the exact order is not defined on (LT/GT, MIN/MAX, SORT/ORDER/BSEARCH).
An operand the Word reads as a String is not one, including an element of JOIN's Vector and TOKENIZE's separator.
AND, NOT, SELECT's mask, or a FILTER predicate block met a value that is not a truth value or Unknown.
An operand the Word reads as a Vector is not one.

CONTRACT was given something other than a Symbol or a block. A name is a Symbol, never a String: no Word turns text into a Symbol (LANG.DICTIONARY.ACYCLIC), so a String asking about a Word is malformed use rather than a lookup that failed.
A higher-order Word's block operand is not a CodeBlock.
DEF or DEL targeted a Core Word or a reserved alias, which the dictionary protects; BIND likewise refuses a reserved name.
The native call-depth guard fired: a pathologically long acyclic call chain reached its nesting limit.
A named internal-computation ceiling other than the step budget was crossed — bigintBits, algebraicTerms, nestingDepth, a numeric literal's digit count, or a program's byte length.

DEF or BIND was refused because what it names would reach itself: a body naming the Word being defined, directly or through other User words, or a bound value naming its own binding, directly or through other bindings — the acyclicity check of LANG.DICTIONARY.ACYCLIC, made when the name is given.

Operands a Word aligns position by position do not align: lifted operands whose shapes neither match nor broadcast (LANG.COLLECTIONS.LIFT), keys and values of different lengths (RECORD, GROUP), rows of different lengths (ZIP), or names that cannot destructure a value (BIND).
A Word was applied with fewer operands than its declared arity.

A Word that assumes its vector operand is in ascending order (BSEARCH) was given one that is not. The order is checked before the search, because a binary search over unordered data would answer something rather than nothing; that the vector is unsorted is the program being wrong about its own data, not data that did not work out.
A name in program text did not resolve to any Word in the compiled-in vocabulary or the live dictionary.

DEL was given a name no User Word holds. The name is DEL's own operand, so this is DEL's condition to declare; a name written in program text that resolves to nothing is unknownWord, which the machine raises before any Word runs.
